importance_ranking.reason: Structure type and service scope are the primary routing gates — a buyer needing a factory shed erection cannot use a canopy or mezzanine contractor. Without these specs, the listing cannot be evaluated for fit.

Project photos are the only evidence of contractor capability and scale — a listing without photos cannot demonstrate whether the contractor has completed industrial shed work or only small canopy jobs. Buyers use photos to verify scale, weld quality, and structural complexity before shortlisting.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Market is fragmented across regional fabrication contractors with no dominant brand; buyers search by capability, certification, and location — not by contractor brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a capital project service with significant on-site execution risk. Buyers evaluate contractor track record, IS:800 compliance capability, NDT certification, years in business, and geographic service reach as primary vendor selection criteria — company credibility is equal in weight to specification fit.

All MS structure contracts are project-quoted after site visit and drawing review; listed price is a budget entry point only. Indian buyers are price-sensitive but final price is always negotiated — price display helps buyers assess whether to engage, not to compare across listings.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Heavy structural fabrication (sheds, trusses, portal frames) is quoted per kg; mezzanine floors and platforms are quoted per sq ft; labour-only erection contracts are quoted per project. Unit must be shown to prevent price misreading across these sub-segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Per kg vs per sq ft vs per project is a genuine ambiguity in this MCAT — buyers cannot interpret or compare indicative prices without knowing the unit basis. Unit display is necessary despite project-based pricing.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what is being built — mezzanine floor, factory shed, industrial shed, warehouse, canopy — which are non-interchangeable applications with order-of-magnitude price differences between them.

Defines the contract scope — turnkey project, erection-only, design-and-build, or repair — which are fundamentally different pricing models and capability requirements that buyers cannot substitute for one another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: IS:2062 E250 vs E350 grade selection drives structural section sizing, load capacity, and fabrication cost — buyers in industrial and oil & gas segments specify grade explicitly in their tender documents.

Span between columns (e.g., 12m, 18m, 24m, 30m) is the primary structural design input that determines section sizes, truss configuration, and fabrication complexity — sellers cannot quote accurately without it.

Primer painting vs hot-dip galvanising vs epoxy coating is a significant cost and durability differentiator — galvanised structures cost substantially more and are specified for corrosive or outdoor environments.

Dead load plus live load specification (per sq m or per sq ft) determines structural section selection and directly drives fabrication weight and cost — without this, sellers cannot produce an accurate BOQ.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Tells the seller what type of structure is needed — factory shed, warehouse, solar structure, lift shaft — routing the RFQ to contractors who specialise in that application and can confirm supply capability.
Defines whether the buyer wants fabrication only, installation only, or full design-and-build — sellers need this to determine their fit and apply the correct pricing model.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Span between columns is the primary structural design input — sellers cannot determine section sizes, truss configuration, or fabrication weight without it, making accurate quoting impossible.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: Buyers commissioning MS structure fabrication typically have site drawings, architectural plans, or reference photos of similar structures they want built. An uploaded drawing or reference image lets sellers assess structural complexity, site constraints, and span configuration before responding — significantly improving quote accuracy and reducing back-and-forth before a site visit.
